_note: ARCHITECT RE-RUN. The implementer's iter-1 sweep is preserved at canopy_invariants_iter1_INVALID.json and is SUPERSEDED — it computed the aim yaw as Atan2(x,z) = 37.66 deg, but BotTreeProbe uses the Atan2(z,x) convention = 52.34 deg (see BotTreeProbe.LineHasTrunkInWindows: x += d*cos(yaw), z += d*sin(yaw)). Its sweep therefore fired 14.68 deg off the tee-to-pin line, into the treeline, which is why it reported a 55.8% trunk block rate at the tee where the correct line gives 0%. It also walked fractions of a single carry from the tee rather than ball positions along the hole, so its 'section1_1_table' did not reproduce SPEC 1.1. The SHIPPED CODE IS UNAFFECTED: VersusBot passes the correct yaw; the defect was confined to the measurement script.

sweep_params.paired_seeds: both samplers draw from an identically-seeded System.Random per trial, so the sample POOL is shared and only the SELECTION differs

assertions.name: clampRate_v2 <= clampRate_order352
assertions.note: Exactly equal — expected. The trunk gate is untouched, so the clamp condition (all samples trunk-blocked) is unchanged by construction. SPEC 1.1's infeasibility risk (a hard canopy reject inflating the clamp rate) did NOT materialise.

assertions.name: meanCanopyContacts_v2 < meanCanopyContacts_order352
assertions.note: 45.6% reduction — 3x larger than the 14.5% the mis-aimed iter-1 sweep reported. Canopy contact is near-eliminated wherever a canopy-free line exists (frac 0.00/0.12/0.25/0.75) and still trims 8-19% in the mid-hole band where SPEC 1.1 measured 100% of lines canopy-blocked.

assertions.name: trunkBlockRate_v2 == trunkBlockRate_order352
assertions.note: Identical by construction: v2 reuses LineHasTrunkInWindows unchanged and applies the canopy score only among already-trunk-clear survivors. Confirmed by the identical clamp rates at every position.

editmode_tests.note: The 3 skips are pre-existing Stage C1 skips in HoleCompleteDriverTests, unrelated to this task.
